questions.q: What is a dashboard, relative to the analyses it contains?
options: A dashboard is a brand-new subject area with its own facts and dimensions
A dashboard is a layout container that arranges already-built analyses onto pages, without rebuilding them
A dashboard replaces the need for the Reports and Analytics catalog
A dashboard can only contain exactly one analysis
questions.explain: Dashboards compose existing analyses into a shared layout; they do not introduce new facts or dimensions of their own.

questions.q: What is the purpose of dashboard "pages"?
options: To store the dashboard-level security settings
To define which subject area the dashboard uses
To act like tabs, so related-but-distinct content doesn't have to compete for space on one screen
To schedule when the dashboard refreshes
questions.explain: Pages let a dashboard separate distinct groupings of content, like an "Aging Overview" page and a "Supplier Detail" page.

questions.q: What does a dashboard-level prompt do, compared to a prompt on an individual analysis?
options: It only affects the first analysis on the page
It permanently changes the underlying analysis definitions
It has no practical effect different from an analysis-level prompt
It applies to every analysis on the dashboard page at once, instead of requiring the same prompt to be set separately on each one
questions.explain: A dashboard-level prompt, such as a single Business Unit selector, filters every analysis on that page simultaneously.

questions.q: Besides the standalone Reports and Analytics catalog, where else can OTBI dashboards and analyses appear?
options: Embedded directly inside a transactional work area, such as the Payables landing page
Nowhere else; they are only viewable in the standalone catalog
Only inside BI Publisher report templates
Only inside Smart View workbooks
questions.explain: Embedded analytics let relevant OTBI content appear directly inside a transactional work area's landing page.

questions.q: Why would a team build several different dashboards (AP team, controller's close, executive summary) that reuse some of the same underlying analyses?
options: Oracle requires a separate dashboard per analysis
Analyses cannot be reused across more than one dashboard
It is not possible to reuse an analysis on more than one dashboard
Different audiences need different combinations and layouts of the same underlying, already-built analyses
questions.explain: Because analyses are built once and dashboards are just composition layers, the same analysis can appear on multiple dashboards tailored to different audiences.
